subject: Materials Science
title: What Is Annealing?
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on What Is Annealing?.

hook.text: Bend a paperclip back and forth — it gets harder until it snaps. That's work hardening.

buildup.text: Cold-working piles up dislocations, making metal harder but also more brittle.

discovery.text: Annealing heats the metal to let atoms rearrange, erasing dislocations and restoring ductility.

twist.text: New strain-free grains nucleate and grow, replacing the damaged structure completely.

climax.text: Without annealing, sheet metal could only be rolled once before cracking apart.

punchline.text: Annealing lets metals forget they were beaten.

quiz.question: What does annealing do to a work-hardened metal?
options: Makes it even harder and more brittle
